title: Functoriality of the inherited sites of fibred groupoids
statement: Fix the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $\mathcal B$ be a site [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], small relative to its sheaves. Let $p:\mathcal X\to\mathcal B$ and $r:\mathcal Y\to\mathcal B$ be categories fibred in groupoids: every base arrow admits a cartesian lift, and every arrow in either total category is cartesian. Here an arrow $a:x'\to x$ over $u:b'\to b$ is cartesian when, for every arrow $z\to x$ over a composite $uv$, there is a unique arrow $z\to x'$ over $v$ whose composite with $a$ is the given arrow. Assume the total categories are also small relative to the sheaf universe. Give $\mathcal X$ and $\mathcal Y$ the covering families consisting of the families whose images in $\mathcal B$ are covering families. These families define sites. Let $F:\mathcal X\to\mathcal Y$ be a functor over $\mathcal B$, compatible with cartesian pullback. Then $F$ preserves covering families and their pullbacks and is continuous and cocontinuous in the sense of [def-weil-pbc-special-cocontinuous-functor]. Explicitly, precomposition with $F^{\mathrm{op}}$ sends sheaves of sets on $\mathcal Y$ to sheaves of sets on $\mathcal X$, and for every covering family $\{y_i\to F(x)\}$ there is a covering family $\{x_i\to x\}$ and isomorphisms $F(x_i)\cong y_i$ over $F(x)$.

source.place: Tags 06NU (lemma-topology-inherited), including its fibred-groupoid specialization immediately following the proof, and 06NW (lemma-topology-inherited-functorial).

proof.text: For either $p$ or $r$, the isomorphism and composition axioms of a site follow directly from the base-site axioms [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology](1): the image of an isomorphism is an isomorphism, and the image of a composite family is the composite of its image families. Reindexing is inherited from the base. Smallness of the total categories in the stated universe ensures that the collection of such families can be taken to be a set, with index sets bounded in that universe.

source.place: Tag 06NU, lemma-topology-inherited, proof (1)-(2) and following fibred-groupoid specialization.

proof.text: Let $\{x_i\to x\}$ be a covering in $\mathcal X$ and let $t\to x$ be any arrow. The base-site axiom gives $P_i=p(x_i)\times_{p(x)}p(t)$ and the covering $\{P_i\to p(t)\}$. Choose a cartesian lift $w_i\to t$ of each second projection. All arrows of $\mathcal X$ are strongly cartesian in the explicit sense of the statement. Thus [lem-sfb-cartesian-lift-pullback-square], with $f=(x_i\to x)$, $g=(t\to x)$ and $a=(w_i\to t)$, makes $w_i$ the pullback $x_i\times_x t$ over $P_i$. The family $\{w_i\to t\}$ is a covering by its base images. This proves the remaining site axiom. Apply the identical argument to $r$ to obtain the site on $\mathcal Y$.

source.place: Tag 06NU, lemma-topology-inherited, proof (3); Categories Tag 06N4, lemma-strongly-cartesian-fibre-product.

proof.text: Since $rF=p$, the image under $F$ of any covering family has exactly the same base covering and hence is a covering. For the pullback square chosen in step 2, $F(w_i)\to F(t)$ is strongly cartesian (every arrow of $\mathcal Y$ is), and lies over $P_i\to p(t)$, while $F(x_i)\to F(x)$ is strongly cartesian over $p(x_i)\to p(x)$. Apply [lem-sfb-cartesian-lift-pullback-square] to these arrows. Its unique upper arrow is $F(w_i\to x_i)$ by the functorial commutativity and its base image. Therefore the actual image square is a pullback, so its canonical comparison with $F(x_i)\times_{F(x)}F(t)$ is an isomorphism. The two defining conditions of continuity [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology](3) now hold.

source.place: Tag 06NW, lemma-topology-inherited-functorial, first paragraph of proof; Categories Tag 06N4.

proof.text: For a covering $\{y_i\xrightarrow{d_i}F(x)\}$ put $U_i=r(y_i)$ and $U=p(x)$. Choose cartesian lifts $a_i:x_i\to x$ of the covering arrows $U_i\to U$. The family $\{a_i\}$ covers $x$. The arrows $F(a_i)$ and $d_i$ are cartesian lifts of the same base arrow with the same target. The cartesian universal properties give $\alpha_i:F(x_i)\to y_i$ and $\beta_i:y_i\to F(x_i)$ over $\mathrm{id}_{U_i}$, with $d_i\alpha_i=F(a_i)$ and $F(a_i)\beta_i=d_i$. Uniqueness in those same universal properties gives $\alpha_i\beta_i=\mathrm{id}$ and $\beta_i\alpha_i=\mathrm{id}$. These are the asserted isomorphisms over $F(x)$, and in particular the image family refines the given covering, which is cocontinuity [def-weil-pbc-special-cocontinuous-functor](1).

source.place: Tag 06NW, lemma-topology-inherited-functorial, second paragraph of proof; Sites Tag 00XJ, definition-cocontinuous.

proof.text: Finally let $G$ be a sheaf of sets on $\mathcal Y$. For any covering $\{x_i\to x\}$, the sheaf equalizer diagram of $G$ for $\{F(x_i)\to F(x)\}$ identifies with the equalizer diagram of $G\circ F^{\mathrm{op}}$ for $\{x_i\to x\}$, using the canonical pullback isomorphisms of step 3. Their projection maps agree because they come from the image squares. The sheaf condition in [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology](1) proves the asserted precomposition statement, including empty covering families.

source.place: Tag 06NW, lemma-topology-inherited-functorial, first paragraph and final assertion; Sites Tag 00WW, lemma-pushforward-sheaf (equalizer argument).
